name: Neutrality May Matter: sentiment in Airbnb, Booking, and Couchsurfing reviews (Brazil/USA)
what_it_holds: Academic paper (Santos, Mota, Benevenuto, Silva; Social Network Analysis and Mining, 2020) that collected and sentiment-scored reviews across three platforms -- Airbnb, Booking.com, and Couchsurfing -- for matched cities in Brazil and the USA. No GitHub code/data repository was found in this pass (search returned only ResearchGate/arXiv/Semantic Scholar mirrors of the paper itself); flagged as a lead worth a direct-author-page or arXiv-supplementary check rather than a confirmed repo.
why_useful: If a companion repo/dataset surfaces, this would be a rare cross-platform (Airbnb vs. hotel-OTA vs. peer-to-peer) matched-city review corpus, useful for a sharing-economy vs. traditional-lodging sentiment/positivity-bias read that could bear on review-count-based demand proxies (why review positivity may differ between Airbnb and Booking, biasing simple review-count comparisons).
themes: Airbnb reviews text corpora and review-date datasets on GitHub (review counts over time as a stays proxy)
why_all: If a companion repo/dataset surfaces, this would be a rare cross-platform (Airbnb vs. hotel-OTA vs. peer-to-peer) matched-city review corpus, useful for a sharing-economy vs. traditional-lodging sentiment/positivity-bias read that could bear on review-count-based demand proxies (why review positivity may differ between Airbnb and Booking, biasing simple review-count comparisons).

name: Replication data for: Racial Discrimination in the Sharing Economy: Evidence from a Field Experiment (Edelman, Luca, Svirsky 2017)
what_it_holds: ICPSR-hosted replication package (not GitHub) for the AEJ: Applied Economics field experiment on Airbnb host acceptance rates by guest race. Covers June-December 2014 audit-study applications data with accept/reject outcomes by host and listing. No GitHub mirror found despite targeted search; flagging as the canonical source location since the paper itself is a foundational Airbnb-adjacent academic dataset (host discrimination behavior, not directly a KPI driver but relevant to platform-trust/regulatory-risk narratives).
why_useful: Not a KPI forecasting input, but a primary source for discrimination/regulatory-risk framing (gap 12 adjacent) and a benchmark dataset if the team ever wants host-acceptance-rate behavior as a trust proxy. Recorded here because no GitHub replication mirror exists -- worth knowing the search came up empty so nobody re-searches this later.
geography: 5 US cities (Baltimore, Dallas, LA, St. Louis, DC per paper)
themes: Academic replication packages using Airbnb data: Zervas Proserpio Byers (hotel impact), Barron Kung Proserpio (housing), Farronato Fradkin, Horn Merante, Garcia-Lopez Barcelona, Koster Los Angeles, Edelman discrimination, Fradkin reviews
why_all: Not a KPI forecasting input, but a primary source for discrimination/regulatory-risk framing (gap 12 adjacent) and a benchmark dataset if the team ever wants host-acceptance-rate behavior as a trust proxy. Recorded here because no GitHub replication mirror exists -- worth knowing the search came up empty so nobody re-searches this later.

Direct primary replication package for one of the eight named papers in this theme; useful as a reference dataset on discrimination/acceptance-rate dynamics even though it predates current forecasting relevance, and as a template for what a proper replication package looks like if the team wants to request similar deposits for the other seven papers.

name: Itloow/lyon-airbnb-discrimination
what_it_holds: 'Analyse NLP des biais discriminatoires dans les annonces Airbnb à Lyon' -- an NLP bias-analysis project on Airbnb listing text for Lyon, France; not a named replication of Edelman/Luca/Svirsky but a student/independent project in the same vein (discriminatory bias in listing text, single city). Updated Jan 2026 (recent). Not inspected further for committed data files.
why_useful: Marginal: a modern (2026), non-US take on discrimination/bias analysis of Airbnb listing text; could be a template for text-bias methodology but is single-city and unlikely to hold a reusable dataset beyond Lyon listings.
themes: Academic replication packages using Airbnb data: Zervas Proserpio Byers (hotel impact), Barron Kung Proserpio (housing), Farronato Fradkin, Horn Merante, Garcia-Lopez Barcelona, Koster Los Angeles, Edelman discrimination, Fradkin reviews
why_all: Marginal: a modern (2026), non-US take on discrimination/bias analysis of Airbnb listing text; could be a template for text-bias methodology but is single-city and unlikely to hold a reusable dataset beyond Lyon listings.

name: Host Concentration & Spatial Clustering in Airbnb: Implications for Urban Housing Sustainability (Nayak, Nayak, Garg 2026)
what_it_holds: Published paper (PDF only, 208KB, CC BY 4.0) in International Journal of Marketing & Financial Management analyzing host concentration, spatial clustering and turnover intensity in NYC using the well-known 2019 Inside Airbnb listing-level dataset we already hold. Zenodo record has only the PDF file, no separate data file.
why_useful: Methodology reference for host-concentration metrics; no new data (duplicates our existing NYC 2019 Inside Airbnb holding).
duplicate_of_holding: Uses the same NYC 2019 Inside Airbnb data we already hold; no new dataset
themes: Airbnb host-side datasets: superhost/multi-listing/professional host panels, host earnings, DAC7 platform-reporting statistics, IRS/tax authority STR income stats
why_all: Methodology reference for host-concentration metrics; no new data (duplicates our existing NYC 2019 Inside Airbnb holding).

name: national_park_visitation_analysis_w_mobile_phone_data
what_it_holds: Replication code for a published Scientific Reports paper (Alba, Pan, Yin et al. 2022) analyzing COVID-19 impact on US national park visitation by race/ethnicity using SafeGraph mobile-phone mobility data at Census Block Group level. Repo holds feature-extraction and modeling scripts under src/; only aggregated outputs are committed (raw SafeGraph data requires a commercial licence, not redistributed).
why_useful: Method/pipeline for turning SafeGraph-style mobility data into park-visitation demand estimates with demographic splits; useful as a template if the team ever gets SafeGraph/Placer.ai access, and as an academic anchor citation for mobility-based destination-demand nowcasting (relates to gap 17, nowcasting methods).
size_hint: code + aggregated results only, no raw mobility rows
themes: Destination demand proxies: US National Park Service visitation stats API, state park attendance, museum/theme-park attendance, ski resort data, beach visitation
why_all: Method/pipeline for turning SafeGraph-style mobility data into park-visitation demand estimates with demographic splits; useful as a template if the team ever gets SafeGraph/Placer.ai access, and as an academic anchor citation for mobility-based destination-demand nowcasting (relates to gap 17, nowcasting methods).
